content: Azelaic acid is a topical medication approved by the FDA for the treatment of mild to moderate rosacea, specifically targeting inflammatory papules and pustules. It is not indicated for the treatment of erythema in the absence of these lesions. Common side effects include itching, stinging, burning, and tingling sensations on the skin. For adults, the recommended dosage of FINACEA Gel, 15%, is to apply a thin layer to the affected areas of the face twice daily, in the morning and evening. Patients should avoid triggers such as spicy foods, hot beverages, and alcohol, and use only mild soaps or soapless cleansers for facial hygiene. If no improvement is observed after 12 weeks of therapy, the treatment should be reassessed. FINACEA Gel, 15%, is contraindicated in individuals with hypersensitivity to propylene glycol or any other component of the formulation. It is intended for dermatologic use only and should not be used in the eyes, mouth, or vagina. Patients with darker skin tones should be monitored for early signs of hypopigmentation, as isolated cases of hypopigmentation have been reported. If severe irritation or sensitivity occurs, the treatment should be discontinued. Adverse reactions reported during clinical trials include burning, stinging, dryness, tightness, scaling, itching, and redness at the application site. Rarely, worsening of asthma, vitiligo, hypertrichosis, and exacerbation of herpes labialis have been reported. Post-marketing reports include facial burning and irritation, as well as iridocyclitis if the gel accidentally comes into contact with the eyes. The safety of azelaic acid during pregnancy has not been fully established. Animal studies have shown embryotoxicity at high oral doses, but no teratogenic effects were observed. The drug should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. In nursing mothers, less than 4% of the topically applied dose is systemically absorbed, and significant changes in milk azelaic acid levels are not expected. However, caution is advised. The mechanism of action of azelaic acid in rosacea is not fully understood. It is a naturally occurring dicarboxylic acid with antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties. The gel formulation contains 15% azelaic acid in an aqueous base with additional excipients such as benzoic acid, disodium EDTA, and propylene glycol. Clinical trials have demonstrated the efficacy of FINACEA Gel, 15%, in reducing inflammatory lesions associated with rosacea. However, its effectiveness in treating erythema without papules or pustules has not been evaluated. Patients should avoid triggers such as spicy foods, hot drinks, and alcohol during treatment. FINACEA Gel, 15%, is supplied in 50 g tubes and should be stored at room temperature (25°C or 77°F), with permissible excursions between 15–30°C (59–86°F). Patients should be instructed to use the gel only as directed, avoid contact with mucous membranes, and wash their hands after application. If excessive irritation occurs, they should discontinue use and consult their physician.
